pr_body:
To fix #4608 issue various things had to be changed.

Every functionality osquery logger can do, is supported using osquery flags and not the GLOG flags. Removed all the flag aliases.
All the GLOG flags which should not be modified are set in separate place(initStatusLogger).
Other configurable GLOG flags are overwritten only in the single case(when FLAGS_v is true)

I had to modify filesystem plugin, as it was completely changing the GLOG configuration. Now, GLOG is configured only in the logger.cpp.

New behavior:
Log files are created in the FLAGS_logger_path folder. When log file exceeded 10 MB new one is created. Log file name matches pattern osqueryd*.SEVERITY*. 
It's now possible to filter out logs completely(set general lower bound of the severity) and also to filter out logs written to stderr(separate severity lower bound for stderr). Other filtering options are not supported by GLOG and if necessary we will have to fork it.

### What version of `osquery` are you using? What operating system. Be specific.

```
osquery_version = 3.2.8
    os_platform = rhel
```

### What have you already tried?

Start osqueryd with
```
osqueryd --logger_plugin=<my_plugin> --logtostderr --logger_min_stderr=2
```
### What did you expect to see?

Should only see `ERROR` level status logs on the console.

### What did you see instead?

Seeing status logs of all levels on the console.
comments:
If logtostderr or alsologtostderr (both are GLOG flags not the osquery flags) are set to true, severity of the log is not considered while printing things to stderr.

However you confusion looks more than understandable. 
1. In command line flags docs osquery and glog flags are mixed.
2. Default values of flag(logtostderr which is GLOG flag and osquery just modifies it) does not match to the default value in the GLOG docs(because of the way osquery modifies it)

And even if you write --logtostderr=false things will not work.

if you write disable_logging=true logtostderr is automatically set to true. 
If you are logging from external process logtostderr is again enabled.
**If logger plugin is not named filesystem logtostderr is automatically enabled https://github.com/facebook/osquery/blob/master/osquery/logger/logger.cpp#L285**


 I will need some time to untangle the code. Reduce number of flags and exactly say what kind of behavior is being changed.

Will assign the issue to myself if you don't mind @fmanco
